summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-react preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as an ESLint configuration but ships a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, at npm install time, downloads the Bun runtime binary from the oven-sh/bun v1.3.13 GitHub release into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and uses it to execute a bundled sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB JavaScript payload whose top level is a shuffled string/opcode array of thousands of entries with a rotator function (`WV8StW`) and hex-renamed locals — the canonical obfuscator.io shape. Neither the runtime fetch nor the obfuscated payload's behavior is documented in the README, and an ESLint configuration has no legitimate need for a secondary language runtime or a large obfuscated payload. Executing the payload under Bun rather than Node bypasses Node-based install-time scanners. The mismatch between the advertised purpose (declarative ESLint config) and the actual install-time behavior (alternate-runtime download plus obfuscated code execution) is consistent with a hijacked publish under the `@ornikar` scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
